projects.title: AgentCeption
projects.tagline: A governed software-execution layer for isolated worktrees, bounded implementation, delivery evidence, and human-reviewed pull-request candidates.
projects.story: AgentCeption receives a bounded software mission contract, validates repository and capability preconditions, performs work in an isolated worktree or equivalent workspace, preserves commands, patches, checks, failures, issues, and artifacts, and returns a delivery packet that may become a pull-request candidate. It never converts execution evidence into automatic merge or deployment authority.
projects.summary: The software-execution role assigned by the PhiOS–Agentora integration lineage. The current public Archive package is an architecture and teaching proof grounded in Agentora v1.0.0 documentation; no standalone public AgentCeption repository or tagged reference runtime is claimed yet.
projects.see: The AgentCeption cover, software delivery lifecycle, review and merge gate, architecture and delivery-boundary briefs, fixed-data Delivery Workbench, PAT Delivery Mode, Agentora integration source lineage, and planned execution contract, reference runtime, and public proof run.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are connected. The Workbench deterministically reviews six bundled synthetic delivery records while accepting no repository, code, file, credential, command, package, URL, or patch and performing no worktree, shell, test, model, network, pull-request, merge, deployment, persistence, or Archive mutation activity.
projects.next: Freeze a portable AgentCeption Execution Contract and Delivery Receipt schema, publish a minimal local-first reference runtime or standalone repository, then conduct Public Delivery Proof 001 against a disposable owner-approved repository with explicit no-merge authority. Publish the base SHA, scope, commands, patch, checks, failures, pull-request state, human decision, and cleanup receipt.
projects.claimBoundary: This package demonstrates AgentCeption public architecture, Agentora integration lineage, and fixed synthetic delivery decisions. It does not establish a public AgentCeption implementation, secure sandboxing, correct worktree or repository isolation, reliable code generation, successful or complete testing, secret protection, supply-chain safety, vulnerability absence, mergeability, deployability, production suitability, organizational permission, human review, completed delivery, or verified software outcomes. Isolation is not security proof, checks are evidence rather than correctness proof, a pull request is a review object rather than merge authority, merge is not deployment, and deployment is not verified success.

relationships.note: Vibe can supply explicit goals, constraints, prohibited effects, and proof surfaces without granting execution, merge, or deployment authority.
PhiOS supplies scoped context and receives proposed continuity writeback; it does not authorize repository actions by itself.
Agentora prepares, launches, refreshes, compares, and reviews software missions while AgentCeption owns the execution path.
SOSA can separate request, security dissent, authorization, operation, review, merge, deployment, and repair judgments.
ALO preserves contracts, commands, patches, checks, failures, decisions, cleanup, merge, deployment, rollback, and outcome continuity.
Census tracks runtime versions, schemas, proof runs, branches, artifacts, receipts, aliases, and publication states.
Archive Core publishes the architecture and synthetic workbench without implying a verified standalone implementation.
